page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM64-based instance powered by an AWS Graviton processor. Specifically, it features the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 CPU architecture with 4 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz, with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m9gd.xlarge demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in specific workloads. It achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.53 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.27 GB/sec, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. However, its overall PassMark CPU score and encryption performance fall into the lower percentiles. Multi-core stress-ng performance and database operations, such as Redis SET operations at 13.22 million operations per second, sit in the average tier. Large-model LLM inference prompt processing is a notable bottleneck, registering in the bottom decile.

The inclusion of a local NVMe SSD instance store combined with dedicated ARMv9 cores offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring fast local scratch space without the overhead of network-attached storage. This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, single-threaded data compression tasks, and lightweight database operations. It is less suitable for heavy cryptographic operations or large-scale LLM inference.
